odor: Faintly sweet at high concentrations; generally odorless at ambient levels
environmentalPersistence: Low — atmospheric lifetime ~1.5 months via OH radical oxidation; near source disperses within hours

lowDose.description: Accelerated ripening/maturation, adventitious root promotion, mild epinasty. Hormetic — can be beneficial for controlled ripening.

highDose.description: Rapid senescence, widespread chlorosis, abscission, stem softening, membrane degradation.

morphologicalEffects.leafSize: Reduced on new growth; existing leaves age faster
morphologicalEffects.leafCurl: Strong downward epinasty — most distinctive morphological effect
morphologicalEffects.chlorosis: Strong — chlorophyllase upregulation causes rapid yellowing
morphologicalEffects.necrosis: Yes at high doses — abscission zone tissue
morphologicalEffects.pigmentation: Mild — yellow-brown tones dominate over anthocyanin
morphologicalEffects.rootGrowth: Inhibited at high doses; adventitious roots stimulated at low doses
morphologicalEffects.stemThickness: Radial swelling at nodes — classic triple response
morphologicalEffects.newVsOldLeaves: Old basal leaves most sensitive — senescence proceeds base upward

physiologyEffects.chlorophyllReduction: Strong — direct upregulation of chlorophyllase and SGR
physiologyEffects.stomatalConductance: Opens at low dose, closes as senescence advances
physiologyEffects.respiratoryBurst: Climacteric respiratory burst — elevated then crashes
physiologyEffects.membranePermeability: Strongly increased — lipid degradation central to senescence

molecularEffects.oxidativeStress: Moderate to high in senescing tissue

microbiomeEffects.fungalEffect: Opportunistic fungi increase on senescing surfaces

temporalDynamics.recoveryTime: 2–3 weeks if brief exposure; chronic exposure causes permanent senescence
temporalDynamics.sensitization: Autocatalytic — ethylene induces its own synthesis; accelerates over time

visualSimulation.colorChanges: Green → yellow (strong) → brown at necrosis zones; minimal purple
visualSimulation.damageSpread: Upward through canopy — base to tip
visualSimulation.damagePattern: Uniform on old leaves, patchy on mid-canopy
visualSimulation.heatmapGlow: Moderate — yellow-toned ACC and chlorophyllase metabolite signature
visualSimulation.microbiomeParticles: Slower, dispersed; slight pathogen fraction increase
visualSimulation.recoveryVisual: Re-greening possible on young leaves if caught early; basal leaves remain scarred

synergies.synergyNote: ET/JA cooperation accelerates senescence and defense simultaneously. ABA + ethylene is the canonical senescence-acceleration pathway.
synergies.antagonismNote: Cytokinins directly oppose ethylene-driven chlorophyll degradation. Auxin suppresses ethylene sensitivity in young tissue.

educationalContext.realWorldSources: Ripening fruit, aging flowers, car exhaust, gas stoves, stressed plant tissue
educationalContext.agriculturalUse: Commercial fruit ripening (bananas, tomatoes); pineapple flowering synchronization
educationalContext.humanToxicity: Not toxic at normal concentrations; simple asphyxiant only at very high levels
educationalContext.climateLink: Ethylene production increases under heat and drought stress — relevant to crop losses under climate change
educationalContext.indoorOutdoor: Both — near ripening fruit indoors; vehicle exhaust outdoors
educationalContext.whyStudentsCare: The molecular reason a banana ripens faster in a bag and why one bad apple spoils the barrel — something every student has observed
educationalContext.realWorldIssue: Food waste, post-harvest crop losses, stress biology under climate change

sources: Abeles FB, Morgan PW, Saltveit ME (1992). Ethylene in Plant Biology, 2nd ed. Academic Press.
Bleecker AB, Kende H (2000). Ethylene: a gaseous signal molecule in plants. Annual Review of Cell and Developmental Biology, 16, 1–18.
Iqbal N, et al. (2017). Ethylene role in plant growth, development and senescence. Frontiers in Plant Science, 8, 937.
